organizations.name: Office of the Secretary of War / Office of the Secretary of Defense (Secretary and Deputy Secretary)

organizations.portfolio: Department-wide acquisition transformation (Portfolio Acquisition Executives, Warfighting Acquisition System), software-acquisition-pathway-by-default policy, requirements reform, direction of flagship AI/C2 programs (Maven program-of-record memo, Advana transformation memo), unmanned-systems consolidation memo.
organizations.current_status_2026: VERIFIED-SEARCH: Budget justification documents for FY2026 and FY2027 are now hosted at comptroller.war.gov, evidencing the Department of War secondary designation. Secretary Pete Hegseth directed the Pentagon-wide acquisition reform (Nov 2025) that replaced PEOs with Portfolio Acquisition Executives in the Army (Nov 7, 2025) and the Air Force (17 portfolios, completed July 2026). Deputy Secretary Steve Feinberg signed the March 9, 2026 memo designating Maven Smart System a program of record and a Jan 12, 2026 Advana transformation memo. RECALL (not re-verified): Hegseth's March 6, 2025 memo 'Directing Modern Software Acquisition to Maximize Lethality' made the Software Acquisition Pathway the default for software and CSOs/OTs the default solicitation approach; an Aug 2025 memo terminated JCIDS in favor of a Requirements and Resourcing Alignment Board and a Mission Engineering and Integration Activity under R&E.

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: DIU posts problem statements under its standing CSO; vendors submit a short solution brief, selected firms pitch, then submit a proposal; awards are prototype OTs (10 USC 4022) with a follow-on production OT available without re-competition if the prototype succeeds. Amendment 0001 (Mar 13, 2026) is the current baseline. In 2026 DIU is narrowing to three priorities and is the front door for the DRPM-UxS unmanned portfolio.
procurement_pathways.typical_award_size: RECALL: low single-digit $M to ~$15M prototype OTs; production follow-ons can reach tens/hundreds of $M (verify against GAO-25-106856).
procurement_pathways.timeline: RECALL: DIU targets 60-90 days from solicitation close to award; solicitation windows typically 2-4 weeks.

recent_examples.company: Public evidence insufficient (2026 C2-specific awardees not retrievable)

procurement_pathways.fit_for_two_founder_startup: MEDIUM-LOW at $250k: DIU wants an existing commercial product with demonstrated traction and the ability to deliver a prototype in months; a pre-product team should first build with SOCOM/NSIN/xTech-type doors and return to DIU with a product.
procurement_pathways.eligibility_notes: OTs carry no US-citizenship ownership test; non-traditional defense contractor status is easy to meet; foreign ownership is permissible but each project may impose security, export (ITAR/EAR) and data-access conditions that a non-US-person founder must be screened against. Needs specialist legal review.

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: CDAO (via Tradewinds assessments or CDAO CSO-style opportunities), DIU, DISA and SOCOM all award prototype OTs. Tradewinds 'awardable' status satisfies competition so any DoD buyer with funds can award quickly; Open DAGIR onboarding can precede an OT.
procurement_pathways.typical_award_size: RECALL: $250k-$5M pilots at CDAO; larger at DISA.
procurement_pathways.timeline: Tradewinds assessment ~30-60 days from monthly close (RECALL); award timing depends entirely on sponsor funding.
procurement_pathways.fit_for_two_founder_startup: HIGH for intake (a 5-minute video is within reach), LOW-MEDIUM for conversion without a sponsor; use it as a credentialing step while hunting a funded user.
procurement_pathways.eligibility_notes: Any vendor may submit; SAM registration required for award; no citizenship ownership test, but ITAR/data-access screening applies per project.

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: Follow-on production under 10 USC 4022(f) after a successful competitively awarded prototype (DIU, CDAO, SOCOM). The Maven scale-up (prototype OT to $1.3B ceiling to program of record) is the archetype.
procurement_pathways.typical_award_size: Tens to hundreds of $M ceilings; obligations far lower and incremental.
procurement_pathways.timeline: Years; requires a prototype success memo (DIU 'Success Memo' construct, RECALL) and a component willing to fund.

recent_examples.what: Maven Smart System prototype scaled to enterprise use, then program of record

procurement_pathways.fit_for_two_founder_startup: Not a starting point; the goal state 3-5 years out.
procurement_pathways.eligibility_notes: Same as prototype OT; production deals attract FOCI/foreign-ownership scrutiny if classified access is needed.

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: OSD, DARPA, DIU-hosted and SOCOM topics appear in the DoD SBIR/STTR BAAs; Phase I ~$150-300k, Phase II ~$1-2M, Direct-to-Phase-II available for some components; OSD topics on C2/AI appear periodically.
procurement_pathways.typical_award_size: Phase I $150k-$300k; Phase II $1M-$2M; D2P2 up to ~$2M (RECALL; verify current DoD SBIR BAA).
procurement_pathways.timeline: 6-9 months from topic release to Phase I award (RECALL).

recent_examples.company: Public evidence insufficient (specific 2026 OSD/DARPA C2 SBIR awardees not retrievable)

procurement_pathways.fit_for_two_founder_startup: MEDIUM for the engineer-led team if eligible; non-dilutive and standard for university spinouts.
procurement_pathways.eligibility_notes: SBIR/STTR requires a for-profit U.S. small business more than 50% owned and controlled by U.S. citizens or permanent resident aliens (or by other such small businesses). With one founder expected to be a permanent resident and one non-U.S.-person founder, the cap table must keep majority ownership/control with U.S. persons; the SBIR/STTR Extension Act of 2022 also requires foreign-affiliation disclosures. Germany and Indonesia are not 'countries of concern', but the ownership test is binding. Needs specialist legal review; do not assume eligibility.

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: DARPA office-wide and program BAAs (STO/I2O) and OSD/R&E BAAs fund research prototypes on resilient C2, autonomy, AI reinforcement; awards are contracts, grants or OTs.
procurement_pathways.fit_for_two_founder_startup: LOW-MEDIUM: technically credible for a strong engineer but slow, IP-encumbered and not a route to a fielded product.
procurement_pathways.eligibility_notes: Foreign participation allowed subject to export control; fundamental-research designation matters for the non-U.S.-person founder's access. Needs legal review.

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: Ride an incumbent: Palantir (Maven/Open DAGIR third-party app, FedStart ATO inheritance - RECALL), SAIC (JFN integrator), Booz Allen (Advana/Thunderdome), or the four JWCC CSPs' marketplaces. The 2026 Maven program-of-record consolidation onto a single Army EA makes 'app on Maven' the dominant joint-level route.
procurement_pathways.timeline: 3-9 months if the prime has a funded need.
procurement_pathways.fit_for_two_founder_startup: HIGH practicality, but strategic dependency on the prime's platform and roadmap.
procurement_pathways.eligibility_notes: Prime flow-downs (DFARS 7012/CMMC, ITAR) apply; a non-U.S.-person founder may be excluded from ITAR technical data unless licensed. Needs legal review.

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: OSD-relevant consortia (e.g., the Information Warfare Research Project and SOSSEC/C5-type consortia - RECALL) issue requests for prototype proposals; membership is inexpensive and awards are OTs executed by the consortium manager.
procurement_pathways.fit_for_two_founder_startup: MEDIUM: cheap to join, but proposals compete with established integrators.
procurement_pathways.eligibility_notes: Consortium membership rules may restrict foreign-owned members; verify each consortium's terms.

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: Not a joint pathway, but SOCOM's SOFWERX (partnership intermediary) plays the equivalent role at the joint/SOF level: assessment events, tech sprints, Small Business Boot Camp, leading to PEO-SDA CSO OTs.
procurement_pathways.timeline: SOFWERX events monthly; OT awards 2-6 months after a successful assessment.
procurement_pathways.fit_for_two_founder_startup: HIGH: lowest-friction joint-level software buyer with real users and IP retention.
procurement_pathways.eligibility_notes: SOF work often requires clearances for on-site integration; the founders' clearance limitations (non-citizen, LPR) constrain which tasks they can perform personally. Needs legal review.

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: For a German founder: Bundeswehr Cyber Innovation Hub, NATO DIANA accelerator, NATO NCIA procurement, and the German Zeitenwende budget offer alternative C2 software buyers; NATO's own Maven adoption (RECALL) shows alliance-level demand for interoperable apps.
procurement_pathways.fit_for_two_founder_startup: MEDIUM: relevant hedge given immigration/ITAR frictions in the U.S. path; covered in depth by the allied-market agent.
procurement_pathways.eligibility_notes: EU/NATO entity requirements; U.S. export controls still apply to U.S.-origin technology.

how_a_startup_gets_in: Sequenced plan for a two-founder, $250k team at the joint/OSD level. (0) Legal pre-work before any submission: structure the cap table so U.S. persons hold >50% ownership and control if SBIR/STTR is wanted; get an export-control classification of the product (ITAR USML XI/XXI vs EAR) and a written plan for the non-U.S.-person founder's technical-data access; decide early whether to pursue a facility clearance (FOCI mitigation would be triggered) or to stay unclassified. (1) Register in SAM.gov and get a CAGE code; prepare an SBOM and SWFT-style assurance artifacts from the first build. (2) Month 1-3, credential cheaply: submit a 5-minute video to the CDAO Tradewinds Solutions Marketplace (monthly windows through May 2027) to obtain 'awardable' status; attend SOFWERX events and the next Small Business Boot Camp; enter NSIN/DIU early-stage programs to find a unit problem owner. (3) Month 3-9, find a funded user, not a policy office: PEO-SDA (SOCOM) CSO for a small prototype OT; CENTCOM REJTF/TF-59/TF-99 for an in-theater trial (contracted through DIU or SOCOM); a service-level door (AFWERX, xTech, Army NGC2 ecosystem, SpaceWERX) if the product maps there. (4) Month 6-12, position inside the platform reality: apply for Open DAGIR onboarding/third-party app status on the Maven data environment and Palantir's startup/ATO-inheritance program, since the 2026 Maven program-of-record decision makes 'app on Maven' the dominant joint route; alternatively subcontract to SAIC on JFN. (5) Month 9-18, scale via OT: convert a successful prototype into a DIU or SOCOM production OT, and pursue GIDE participation via the CDAO sponsor. (6) Avoid: DISA/JWCC/Thunderdome direct pursuit, OSC loans, and DARPA as a first revenue source. (7) Hedge: NATO DIANA/Bundeswehr routes for the German founder. Throughout, track the DIU three-priority narrowing (autonomy/lethality emphasis) and DRPM-UxS: a C2 product that controls or tasks unmanned systems has a clearer joint-level sponsor in 2026 than a generic staff COP.
